head: 7cdebfb2d9bd2a2fcf98b22e4ab559be94e362a9
method: Independent viewing of original-size 12 fps decoded frames, using at/hit/duration and visible labels. Each assigned skill checked at start/middle, adjacent impact frames and tail. No phone operation or runtime/test edits.
scope: Eight assigned skills; static review already passed. Only concrete dynamic jump/crop/identity/alignment/HUD/over-shrink regressions assessed.

rows.observation: Small gold-brown protective rim gathers around the caster lower body, stays at the same recipient and fades in place. Shield ring remains identifiable; face and HP remain readable. Warm orange highlight resembles fire at peak but is a source color preference, not a new sequence regression.

Broad sand-and-rock spiral changes into multiple ground eruptions across the same battlefield region, then disperses. Adjacent519/520 preserve spatial region during topology change; no emitter relocation or hard viewport cut. Central portrait briefly obscured at impact, HP bars retained. Existing large area silhouette retained; no further enlargement recommended.

Cyan-green transparent envelope forms around caster, breaks into thin arcs and dissolves locally. Adjacent546/547 show expected dissolution, no position jump. Portrait remains visible; effect does not swallow neighbors or hide HP.

Concentrated rock mass becomes vertical ground strike and fragmented shock at the same enemy. Adjacent571/572 retain the impact anchor while rock silhouette breaks apart; localized peak portrait coverage is expected. Tail fades, HP remains readable.

Rock energy resolves into a diagonal slash, then short local rock burst and fade. Adjacent596/597 retain burst center during alpha reduction. No visible border clipping, recipient drift or excessive shrinking; HP remains readable.

Wind spiral becomes a recognizable fist and local burst; adjacent615/616 change into a circular wind tail without translating to another unit. Strong impact briefly covers target portrait, HP stays above it; tail clears.

Two curved wind blades resolve into a bright X at recipient, then X fades locally. Adjacent639/640 keep center stable. X extends behind HUD but text and red HP are still readable; no viewport clip or undersized identity.

Wind cone and blue lightning converge into a compact radiant strike then fade at recipient. Adjacent665/666 retain center and identity through impact. No visible crop, adjacent-recipient obstruction or persistent tail; HP remains readable.

decision: No new blocking dynamic defect observed in assigned eight samples. Preserve accepted sources and geometry; stop additional art refinement for these items.
limitations: 12 fps sampling cannot certify every display frame or FPS performance.
QA selection border and browser/label overlays are fixture UI.
Results apply to captured formation and cast sample, not exhaustive every side/recipient topology validation.
A bright impact may briefly cover its intended portrait; no requirement that every effect retain a perfectly centered white point.
